assumptions: THIS INCREMENT IS THE SQL-LEXER BATCH: tooling and static tests only, NO MIGRATION and NO DEPENDENCY, so no migration number and no RFC is needed. Plan a0-batch-sql-lexer-plan-2026-10-03.md and disposition product-owner-disposition-2026-10-03-batch-sql-lexer.md. It decides nothing beyond the recommendation the Owner accepted and approves no RFC.
The lexer follows PostgreSQL 17 lexical rules with standard_conforming_strings on; any mention of that setting stays refused by psqlLex, so the other reading never applies to a fed source.

A text EXECUTE, a DO block or a function body runs WHOLE is valid SQL or runs nothing (a syntax error stops it before execution), so reading every literal and dollar body as SQL, at every level to depth 8, reads every statically spelled statement a fed source can run; text computed at run time is outside, as stated.

security_privacy_cost_impact: Security: tooling and static tests only; no grant, policy, role or schema change. Every static reader now reads SQL as PostgreSQL does, and psqlLex refuses in every fed source, at every level of literal and dollar body: COPY to or from any target but STDIN/STDOUT whatever its quoting (C0-OTR-2, A1-RC-1, Q0-OT2-1), a server-file function called by name or internal symbol, LANGUAGE internal or c (A1-RC-2), CREATE EXTENSION outside pgcrypto and the foreign-data statements (Q0-OT2-2). Each was reachable only by a reviewed migration author; the live catalog probes still hold the guarantees. Privacy: no data. Cost: none; no dependency. Review round: a server-file function is refused as ANY identifier token outside GRANT, REVOKE or COMMENT (C0-SL-1: an operator over lo_export and a rename of it each wrote a host file with every layer green before), and every `;` psql would hold inside CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE is refused (C0-SL-3).

known_limitations: Semantics are not lexical: which function a name resolves to, what a body does at run time, whether a grant widens anything. The live catalog probes hold these.
Text computed at run time (EXECUTE of a concatenation, format(), chr(), set_config of a built name, 'pro' || 'gram') is not read by any lexer.
The word rules over the lexer's output (the tripwire and view patterns, the migration-text pins) are still patterns, over normalised text, and read the spellings pinned.
The differential is re-checked statically only for sources whose sha256 it recorded; a new fed source needs the measurement re-run (owed to A0 on open_blockers[185]).
A psql variable reference named by a digit (b[1:2]) is admitted: psql sets none and nothing fed can set one.

evidence/VERIFICATION.md was written with record-verification.mjs's own render at 685/685/0, because record:verification refuses while the handoff guard is red and the handoff commit is last and alone; verification-record.test.mjs checks it against a live run.

A literal holding only a server-file name (`where proname = 'lo_export'`) is refused, because a literal's text is read as SQL at the next level: an over-refusal, fail closed, that no fed source meets today.
A `;` psql's begin_depth heuristic would hold is refused, not modelled: modelling the merge would hide a later statement's head from the transaction-control rule.
Word rules over raw or stripped text remain in rls-assertions.test.mjs (set_config over the helper) and the §8.5 rules of run.mjs (C0-SL-I2), within the stated word-rule limit.
